payload.explanation_text: Cell membranes are made of phospholipids, which have a water-loving head and two water-avoiding tails. In water they line up in two layers with the tails tucked inside. (Example text; the real Tutor writes the full explanation.)

concepts.name: Amphipathic phospholipids form the bilayer
concepts.taught_summary: Heads face the water and tails face inward, forming a two-layer membrane.

concepts.name: Saturated vs. unsaturated fatty acids
concepts.taught_summary: Saturated tails pack tightly; kinks from double bonds in unsaturated tails increase fluidity.

concepts.name: Cholesterol as a fluidity buffer
concepts.taught_summary: Cholesterol keeps the membrane from becoming too fluid when warm or too stiff when cold.
